This holds true regardless of the specific colormap index selected, as the multiplication by zero nullifies the color contribution.

This maps the cyclic phase to an integer index in the colormap [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly describes the implementation of a cyclic colormap mapping. Specifically, the code snippet `cmap_index = (torch.atan2(imag_part, real_part).div(math.tau).add(0.5).mul(degree).multiply(cyclic_colourmap.shape[0]).floor().long().remainder(cyclic_colourmap.shape[0]))` calculates an integer index based on the argument (phase) of the complex number. The formula `(arg(z) / 2pi + 0.5) * degree * N` maps the cyclic phase (angle) to an integer index within the bounds of the colormap length `N`. This directly supports the claim that the cyclic phase is mapped to an integer index in the colormap.
